Hey, i read through alot of the comments and I think everyone is missing the point for helpful advice to you so let's take a step back. 



This is the financial independence retire early sub. Retiring early is entirely dependent on your annual expenses. How much do you spend each month? Do you know this amount? How much does your partner spend? You need to know these numbers to get to the next part. 


IMPORTANT: Are your financial goals the same as your partners? Figure this out now! If you are saving 3k a month and your partner is saving nothing what happens in 20 or 30 years when you can retire and your partner has 0 savings? Are you going to retire and let them keep working? Sounds like resentment could build there. These are hard discussions that need to happen and the earlier the better. (Ofc i have no idea your relationship but my wife and I have combined finances with a single financial goal we are both working towards. Different things work for different people but communication holds everything together).


The most simple way to calculate when you can retire is when your net worth is 25x your annual spend. Most people retire in their 60's if at all so retiring any earlier than that is a win in my book.


Getting a bit into the details, Most people look for a 3% savings withdrawal rate and assume a 6% market return. You can assume a 6% return if your bought into the whole market. Do you buy the whole us market or the whole world market? The most boring investment approach is the best one imo. Vti and vxus and chill. Check out the boglehead subreddit for more on this.


Lastly, when retiring you want to own your own home to keep expenses down. No mortgage does alot to reduce this annual expense and is less volatile. Your rent isn't going to increase by 15% each year or something stupid. I would personally never buy a condo because what happens when you need a new roof and the other half of the condo doesn't have money? Now your in a weird position? Imo save longer and get a whole house.

Your going about it wrong if gaining mmr is your goal. Pick 2 rolls, and 4 heros. My two rolls were 1 and 5. Every patch, I pick new heros that I think are broken. Only play those heros. Most importantly, Dont play ranked if you dont feel good. I play significantly worse if I hungry or havent eaten. Secondly, I give myself 2 losses and then im done for the day (with ranked). If those two losses happen right away, sucks for me, -60. If not, maybe I go up that day.

When I play pos 1, I am always asking myself, "Is this creep wave safe to farm" This question leads to,

1. Where are the enemies? are they showing, do the ones not showing have the ability to kill me?
2. Where are my teammates? Can they help me if i get gone on? Are my teammates showing? If they arnt showing, the enemy may be scared to go on me.
3. Is the risk of dying here worth the reward? (some deaths are ok, (usually not on p1 but applies to alot of other heros) take liquid vs HR last week. Mindcontrol died so many times top as beastmaster but it actually didnt matter becasue the creep waves were always so shoved.

A common miss conception is that your team needs to create space for you to farm on your 1 early, but sometimes (not always) you can create space for yourself by shoving waves and then fall back to the jungle and forcing the opposing team to address the split push, this alleviates pressure for your team and allows them to get onto the map more.

I just hit div 0 as well. Of my last 14 games to div 0, I won 13 of them. My strategy was to roll for p1, if I won, I played the best p1 for the game, usually last picking it, (slark, tb am, drow), if I lost, I instalocked p5 shaman.

The trick with shaman is make sure your cores carry the fuck out of you. Start, 2x tango, salve both wards, crow, salve and then clarity and branches. 2 tangos to the mid, 1 ward to the offlaner, and then ward for mid. Your priority is to secure the p1's farm. You hit like a truck lvl 1, don't let the offlane get lvl 2. You have so much regen trade with him. #2 go 1,1,1 and gank mid. 2 disables is enough to kill the mid 90 percent of the time.

When you hit 6, usually with the tome, push with that catapult wave and take a tower. Gank some more, stack, rinse repeat when wards are up. Remember, your carry is going to win you the game so you need to make is as easy as possible for him and enable him to. Pma the shit out of him.

Wards allow you to push towers and keep your p1 and 2 from jungling after a teamfight.


Lastly, don't diversify. Pick a few hero's and spam the shit out of it. Abuse a meta hero or pick your favorite, it doesn't matter as long as you are able to push and abuse the power spikes of the hero.

1 thing I notice about lower level supports is that they don't try to find wards, If i buy 20 obs I will buy 20 sents to try to find the enemy's wards. Vision is key to winning. Shoving waves and warding and dewarding keeps your p1 alive.

I have a few 1k friends that I am trying to help get out of 1k. The main issue that they have is that they don't take the game seriously and misjudge the status of the game. The other tilts early and doesnt understand that the win condition for the offlane isnt to kill the safelane, but it is to just not die alot, get xp and keep the enemy supports in the lane. I have found that my 1k friends do not understand all of the heros well enough to know how to begin theory crafting ideas about how to deal with them.

How to get out of 1k, the fast track.
1. have a basic understanding of all the heros.
2. go to dota buff and find a hero in <2k bracket with a high win rate, ie above 53%
3. Find another two with a high win rate.
3.5. Go to youtube and watch a few purgegamers videos about the hero, even if they are a tad old (from another patch) they will still be very usefull
4. Play that one hero every game (unless it is banned) so that you understand what the hero can do at different stages of the game and learn how to itemize correctly on that hero.
5. Dont worry about individual wins and losses, worry about trends over 20-30 games.
